inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average shares, Q2 2026 10-Q (386.0M; XBRL WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding). Held FLAT because SBC plus equity-award withholding taxes are fully expensed in the flows; charging dilution as well would double-count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement: ShareBasedCompensation $243M plus PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation $149M (financing) = $392M. Stryker publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC line, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.9 -> cost of equity ~8.8%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.0% (FY2025 interest expense $607M on ~$16B average debt), ~3.2% after tax. Market weights ~88% equity ($105B) / 12% debt ($14.9B) -> ~8.1%; rounded up to 8.25%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged through the scenario paths and weights, not a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases (~$205M/yr expense, $504M liability at 2026-06-30) sit inside operating expense and therefore inside EBITDA; the lease liability is NOT added to net debt. One treatment, charged once.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md as a US operating company (medical devices: MedSurg & Neurotechnology + Orthopaedics). No prior DCF and no MEMORY.md entry -- first valuation. Not non-US, no FX, no NCI, SBC is material (not SBC-zero), so owner-fcf-adaptations.md was not required. FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end); year 1 of the projection is FY2026, which is already half reported (H1 revenue $12,609M, +6.1% reported; Q1 hit by the March-2026 cyberattack, Q2 +9.4%). Net debt is at 2026-06-30 (debt $750M current + $14,192M non-current = $14,942M; cash $3,391M + $85M current AFS debt securities), so roughly $0.3B of H1-2026 debt paydown overlaps the FY2026 flow -- under $1/share, accepted. INTEREST INCOME: $121M FY2025 is not stripped because the company is net-debt (net cash not material); the build is unlevered and net debt is deducted at the bridge. GROWTH is modelled ORGANIC (guidance 8.3-9.3% organic for FY2026) and acquisition spend is NOT deducted; Stryker is a serial acquirer (Inari $4.9B in 2025, ~$0.46B in H1 2026), so any M&A-driven revenue above these paths would have to be paid for in cash not in this model. EBITDA margin is GAAP EBITDA plus SBC (engine deducts SBC separately): FY2025 (6,459+243)/25,116 = 26.7%; H1-2026 (3,394+141)/12,609 = 28.0%. GAAP special items (restructuring, integration, recall/legal) are left in -- Stryker has them every year, so they are treated as a recurring cost rather than adjusted away; this is why the margin path sits ~3pp below the company's 'adjusted operating margin' framing (27.4% in Q2-26 before D&A). D&A 6.25% of revenue in FY2025 includes $732M of acquired-intangible amortization that runs off (schedule: $715M next 12m, ~$600M by year 5); the path glides D&A toward ~3.6%, just above capex, so the terminal year does not capitalize a tax shield from intangibles that only continued M&A would replenish. Working capital is negative capture (inventory- and receivables-heavy device maker: growth consumes cash). BUYBACKS: zero since FY2020 ($307M FY2019 last); FY2025 $1.03B authorization remaining and management signalled resumption in H2-2026 -- the flat count is currently a modelling convention not yet funded (diluted count drifted 380.3M FY2020 -> 386.0M).
inputs.data_sources_note: XBRL companyfacts (CIK 310764) pulled 2026-10-02 for debt split, AFS securities, equity-award taxes, interest income, intangible amortization schedule and diluted share count.

historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding taxes): FY2020 2,538; FY2022 1,746; FY2025 3,891 ($M). The 3-year FCF CAGR (30.6%) runs from a FY2022 working-capital/supply-chain trough and is not a forward rate; the 5-year (8.9%) is the honest one. Owner and reported 5-year FCF CAGRs match, so SBC is not outgrowing cash flow. Revenue, EPS and equity CAGRs all include acquisitions (Wright Medical FY2020, Vocera FY2023, Inari FY2025) -- the 11.4% selected equity CAGR overstates organic capacity, so projected growth starts from the FY2026 ORGANIC guidance (8.3-9.3%) instead. EPS 5-year CAGR flattered by a COVID-depressed FY2020 base (4.26).

base.rationale: FY2026 8.0% reported growth sits just under the 8.8% organic-guidance midpoint because H1 printed +6.1% and the guide needs ~11% in H2; then a glide from high-single-digit to 4% as Mako/Inari tailwinds mature. Margin expands ~50-60bp/yr (company has delivered ~100bp/yr adjusted, partly offset by MedSurg mix shift) to 30.5% pre-SBC GAAP EBITDA.

bull.rationale: Top-of-guidance FY2026 then sustained ~9% organic as Mako extends to spine/shoulder and Inari cross-sells; operating leverage reaches 32.5%.

bear.rationale: Guide missed after the cyberattack, robotics share loss and mix shift hold growth to mid-single digits; tariffs and MedSurg mix absorb all productivity so margins stall at ~27.5%.

scenario_narratives.base: Stryker lands FY2026 near, but slightly under, its 8.3-9.3% organic guide: Q2's +9% organic shows the March cyberattack was a timing disruption, but H1 reported growth of only 6.1% leaves a demanding H2. From there the two engines -- Mako robotic placements pulling through knee/hip/shoulder implants, and MedSurg & Neurotechnology (Inari venous thromboembolism, neurovascular, endoscopy, medical beds/stretchers) -- keep organic growth high-single-digit for several years before maturing toward 4%. Mix shift toward the lower-gross-margin MedSurg segment caps the margin gain at ~50-60bp/yr, ending at ~30.5% pre-SBC GAAP EBITDA. No buybacks are assumed to create value (the flat count is held by expensing SBC); M&A is excluded, so growth is organic only.
scenario_narratives.bull: Mako's ~2,700-system installed base widens its lead over Zimmer's ROSA and J&J's VELYS as spine and shoulder applications launch, keeping Orthopaedics growing mid-to-high single digit and lifting implant mix; Inari is cross-sold through Stryker's hospital relationships and the VTE market grows double-digit. Low China exposure (~2%) shields Stryker from VBP and tariff escalation relative to peers. Organic growth holds ~9% through 2030 and operating leverage plus manufacturing productivity take pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 32.5%. Market re-rates toward its historic premium multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: The cyberattack proves more than a timing issue -- lost capital-equipment orders and hospital trust push FY2026 below guide -- while ROSA and VELYS close the robotics gap and hospital capex budgets tighten. MedSurg (lower margin) keeps outgrowing Orthopaedics, tariffs (~$175M in FY2025, unquantified for 2026) recur, and legacy hip litigation (MDL 2768/2441) and post-Inari leverage absorb cash. Growth decays to ~3% and margins stall at ~27.5%; the market pays a mid-teens FCF multiple for a slower, ex-premium medtech.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 20% because H1-2026 reported growth (6.1%) lags the 8.3-9.3% organic guide and the stock sits near its 52-week low with sell-side targets being cut, so the market is pricing a credible miss; the bear is margin and growth, not solvency (net debt ~1.6x EBITDA). Base 50% as the guided path. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs both a robotics-share win and sustained margin expansion against an acknowledged mix headwind.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Unlevered owner-FCF DCF with SBC plus equity-award withholding taxes fully expensed and the diluted count held flat. Growth is organic only; acquisitions are neither modelled nor charged. GAAP special items are treated as recurring costs. Acquired-intangible amortization is run off so the terminal tax shield is not perpetuated.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value is the majority of EV; a 1pp WACC change moves value roughly 15-20%.
M&A is excluded: Stryker's history of buying growth means reported revenue will likely outrun these organic paths, but at a cash cost this model does not charge.
FY2026 H2 must deliver ~11% growth to meet guidance after a cyberattack-hit Q1.
Robotics competition (ROSA, VELYS) and MedSurg mix shift both cap margin expansion.
Legacy hip-implant litigation and tariffs are unquantified cash risks.
